title: EACH PART, ITS FUNCTION
about: A cartel boss comes to a Texas ranch gate for his shipment and gets a civics lesson instead: Walter sorts every man into a part of the soul, and the part called appetite ends up in the canyon.

beats.text: A Texas ranch at sunset. A marble Socrates stands in the pasture, a former civics teacher waits at the gate in a breastplate, and an armored cartel truck rolls up the dirt road.
see: a big truck on a dirt road

beats.text: You put a statue in a cow field like it's a church.
It is a church.
You took land I pay for. You're running product through my routes. And you're telling my people you're a state.
Not a state. A polis.
Behind Walter, in the shade of a windmill, three hundred men stand perfectly still with spears and rifles. He calls them his guardians.
see: men standing in rows beside a windmill

beats.text: Mateo makes his offer. Hand over the shipment, and Walter's family keeps breathing. Walter answers the only way he knows.
see: a man in a cowboy hat at a ranch gate

beats.text: I taught civics. This is the only way I know how to threaten someone. Justice is each part of the soul performing its proper function.
That sounds like a slogan.
It's a diagnosis. You are appetite. Your function is to take. To consume. To turn fear into profit.
Walter's partner, he says, is spirit: loyalty, bravery, and anger when necessary.
see: a young man in a cap

beats.text: Bro, I'm also like... sadness and stuff.
I'm reason. My function is to decide what lives... and what doesn't.

beats.ask: somebody has to make the decisions

beats.text: Reason doesn't get to play god.
In Texas, everyone plays god. Some of us just finally admit it.
Mateo says Walter is outnumbered. Walter steps aside. Past the gate is a narrow canyon, and the truck has stopped right at its edge.
see: a truck parked at the edge of a ravine

beats.text: This is a set-up.
No. This is education.
The three hundred charge downhill. They knock the rifles aside, wedge their spears under the trailer, and roll the truck into the canyon.
see: a truck lying on its side in a ditch

beats.text: You think this makes you righteous?
No. It makes me inevitable.
This isn't over.
Nothing ever is.
Mateo backs away to his last pickup. Walter looks out over the cattle, the dust and the smoke. He does not smile.
see: cattle in a field at sunset

beats.ask: I don't think anyone really won

beats.text: Dude... we just flipped a semi with, like... feelings.
No. We flipped it with function.
